bib.title: Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision

question: Can a simple dual-encoder trained with a contrastive loss on over a billion noisy alt-text image pairs, with minimal filtering, yield state-of-the-art visual and vision-language representations?
hypothesis: Scale of the corpus can make up for its noise, so heavy curation is not needed.
contributions: ALIGN: dual-encoder (EfficientNet + BERT) trained with a normalized-softmax contrastive loss on 1.8B noisy alt-text pairs
SOTA zero-shot and fine-tuned image-text retrieval on Flickr30K, MSCOCO and CxC
Zero-shot ImageNet classification and strong image-encoder transfer (ImageNet, VTAB, fine-grained)
Cross-modal and image+text query search; multilingual variant

method.summary: A pair of encoders (EfficientNet-L2 image, BERT-Large text, [CLS] embedding plus linear layer) is trained from scratch with symmetric in-batch normalized softmax loss and a learned temperature on 1.8B alt-text pairs filtered only by frequency and size. It is evaluated zero-shot and fine-tuned on retrieval, zero-shot and transfer on classification.
method.task: contrastive image-text pre-training; cross-modal retrieval; image classification transfer

datasets.name: ALIGN noisy alt-text corpus (English)
datasets.source: raw English alt-text following Conceptual Captions pipeline; not released
datasets.preprocessing: Remove porn, keep images with shorter side >200 px and aspect ratio <3, drop images with >1000 alt-texts; drop alt-texts shared by >10 images, with tokens outside the 100M most frequent uni/bigrams, or <3 or >20 unigrams; near-duplicates of test images removed (Appendix A: k-means 4K clusters, top-10 clusters, cosine >0.975)

datasets.name: ImageNet ILSVRC-2012 and variants R, A, V2
VTAB (19 tasks)
datasets.size: 1000 train images per task (800 train, 200 val for sweep)

datasets.name: Oxford Flowers-102, Oxford-IIIT Pets, Stanford Cars, Food101

models.name: ALIGN (EfficientNet-L2 + BERT-Large)
models.architecture: dual encoder, cosine similarity; EfficientNet with global pooling (1x1 conv of classification head not trained) and BERT [CLS] + linear layer

other.embedding_dim: 1376 for L2 (640 for B7 and baseline ablation)
other.image_resolution: 289x289 train (resize 346 then random crop + flip), central crop eval

training.objective: sum of image-to-text and text-to-image normalized softmax losses over in-batch negatives, label smoothing 0.1, embeddings gathered across all cores, learnable temperature shared (init 1.0)
training.optimizer: LAMB (tried SGD momentum and Adam, LAMB better)
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup then linear decay to zero

other.finetune_retrieval: global batch 2048, initial lr 1e-5, 3K steps (Flickr30K) and 6K steps (MSCOCO), linear decay, other hyperparameters as pre-training
other.imagenet_transfer: batch 1024, SGD momentum 0.9, lr decay x0.2 every 30 epochs, 100 epochs, wd 0, lr 0.1 frozen / 0.01 finetune with 10x smaller on backbone; train/eval res 289/360 frozen, 475/600 finetune
other.finegrained_transfer: batch 256, wd 1e-5, lr 1e-2 then 1e-3, cosine decay over 20k steps, res 289/360, BN stats frozen
other.vtab: 50-trial sweep per task, mean of three runs

inference.samples: Fine-grained and VTAB: average of three runs; other tables single-run, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot classification uses CLIP's prompt templates (e.g. 'A photo of a {classname}'), embeddings averaged then L2-normalized; ensembling gives +2.9% ImageNet top-1
inference.retrieval: cosine similarity of normalized embeddings; demo index of 160M CC-BY images; image+text query adds normalized embeddings with text weight 2, image weight 1

metrics.name: Recall@K
metrics.definition: fraction of queries with the ground truth in top K, image->text and text->image

metrics.name: Spearman R x100 (STS, SIS, SITS)
metrics.definition: correlation with human similarity judgments, bootstrap

metrics.name: mean Recall (mR)
metrics.definition: average of R@1, R@5, R@10 over image->text and text->image

metrics.name: ImageNet KNN R@1
metrics.definition: for each validation image, retrieve nearest training images; hit if label appears in top K

eval.protocol: Mostly single runs; VTAB and fine-grained report three runs; CxC Spearman has bootstrap std; ablations at 1M steps on MSCOCO zero-shot and ImageNet KNN.

availability.data: not released; dataset built from raw alt-text, not obtainable from paper

prompts.purpose: zero-shot ImageNet class prompt (one of CLIP's templates)

evidence.quote: We train the model on 1024 Cloud TPUv3 cores with 16 positive pairs on each core. Therefore the total effective batch size is 16384.

results.claim: Zero-shot ImageNet top-1 of ALIGN, on par with CLIP
results.setup: ALIGN EfficientNet-L2 + BERT-Large, class names fed to text encoder with CLIP prompt ensembling
results.quote: achieving 76.4% top-1 accuracy in ImageNet without using any of its training samples

results.claim: Zero-shot Flickr30K text-to-image R@1 beats CLIP by 7 points
results.setup: Zero-shot, Flickr30K 1K test, ALIGN vs CLIP
results.table: Table 1, Flickr30K zero-shot, row ALIGN, text->image R@1 (75.7) vs CLIP (68.7)

results.claim: Zero-shot Flickr30K image-to-text R@1 is 88.6 vs CLIP 88.0, a small edge
results.table: Table 1, Flickr30K zero-shot, row ALIGN, image->text R@1 (88.6) vs CLIP (88.0)

results.claim: Zero-shot MSCOCO 5K image-to-text R@1 is 58.6 vs CLIP 58.4; text-to-image 45.6 vs 37.8
results.table: Table 1, MSCOCO zero-shot, row ALIGN, image->text R@1 (58.6) and text->image R@1 (45.6); CLIP 58.4 and 37.8

results.claim: Fine-tuned Flickr30K image-to-text R@1 of ALIGN
results.table: Table 1, Flickr30K fine-tuned, row ALIGN, image->text R@1 (95.3), text->image R@1 (84.9)

results.claim: Fine-tuned MSCOCO image-to-text R@1 77.0, text-to-image 59.9
results.setup: Fine-tuned on MSCOCO 82K train + 30K val, 5K test
results.table: Table 1, MSCOCO fine-tuned, row ALIGN, image->text R@1 (77.0), text->image R@1 (59.9)

results.claim: Dataset size of 1.8B noisy alt-text pairs with only frequency filtering
results.quote: The result is a much larger (1.8B image-text pairs) but noisier dataset.

results.claim: ImageNet top-1 with frozen features 85.5, fine-tuned 88.64
results.setup: ALIGN EfficientNet-L2 image encoder; frozen features then full fine-tune, 475/600 train/eval resolution fine-tuning
results.table: Table 5, row ALIGN (EfficientNet-L2), columns Acc@1 w/ frozen features and Acc@1 (85.5, 88.64)

results.claim: VTAB 19 tasks mean accuracy 79.99 vs BiT-L 78.72
results.setup: 1000 training images per task, 50-trial sweep, mean of three fine-tuning runs
results.table: Table 6, row ALIGN, column All tasks (79.99±0.15); Bit-L 78.72

results.claim: CxC image-to-text R@1 78.1 vs 55.9 for best prior (+22.2)
results.setup: MSCOCO fine-tuned ALIGN evaluated on Crisscrossed Captions
results.table: Table 2, row ALIGN, column image->text R@1 (78.1); DET2T+I2T 55.9

results.claim: Same-modality CxC retrieval improves less: text-to-text R@1 45.4 vs 42.4, image-to-image 49.4 vs 44.2
results.table: Table 2, row ALIGN, columns text->text R@1 (45.4) and image->image R@1 (49.4)

results.claim: On CxC semantic similarity, ALIGN is worse than VSE++ on STS and than DEI2T on SIS, but best on SITS and mean
results.note: Text says STS and SIS are 'slightly worse than VSE++ and DEI2T', but Table 3 shows SIS 77.2 above VSE++ 73.3 and DET2T+I2T 74.5; only DEI2T (81.3) is higher for SIS, and STS 72.9 trails VSE++ 74.4 and DET2T+I2T 74.2.
results.quote: Table 3 shows that ALIGN also outperforms the previous SOTA on SITS task with an improvement of 5.7%.

results.claim: Authors attribute weaker intra-modal results to the cross-modal-only training objective
results.quote: We suspect it is because the training objective of ALIGN focuses on cross-modal (image-text) matching instead of intra-modal matching.

results.claim: With 3M noisy ALIGN pairs, MSCOCO zero-shot image-to-text R@1 is 8.1 vs 18.9 for cleaned CC-3M; 12M noisy pairs reach 23.8
results.setup: B7 + BERT-base trained from scratch; subsets randomly sampled from ALIGN data
results.note: Text says ALIGN outperforms CC 'with only 4x size': 12M vs 3M.
results.table: Table 10, rows ALIGN 3M data (8.1), CC-3M data (18.9), ALIGN 12M data (23.8), column I2T R@1

results.claim: Full ALIGN data vs CC-3M on B7+BERT-base: MSCOCO I2T R@1 55.4 vs 18.9
results.setup: Zero-shot MSCOCO retrieval; CC-3M trained with 1/10 of default steps
results.table: Table 9, row B7 + BERT-base + ALIGN full data vs + CC-3M data, column I2T R@1

results.claim: 10% of ALIGN data nearly saturates the small B3+BERT-mini model but not B7+BERT-base
results.table: Table 9, B3 + BERT-mini ALIGN full data 37.4 vs 10% 36.7; B7+BERT-base 55.4 vs 52.0 (I2T R@1)

results.claim: Fewer in-batch negatives degrade quality: 25% negatives gives I2T R@1 48.7 vs 51.7
results.table: Table 8, rows B5 + BERT-base (51.7) and w/ 25% in-batch negs (48.7), column I2T R@1

results.claim: Learned temperature converged to about 1/64; fixed 1/32 is much worse (I2T R@1 39.6)
results.quote: Compared to the baseline model that learns the temperature parameter (converged to about 1/64), some hand-selected, ﬁxed temperatures could be slightly better.

results.claim: Embedding dimension 80 drops I2T R@1 to 42.0 vs 51.7 at 640
results.table: Table 8, row w/ embedding dim=80, column I2T R@1

results.claim: Multilingual ALIGN zero-shot Multi30K mean recall: de 84.1, fr 84.9, cs 63.2, en 90.2 (English-only model 92.2)
results.table: Table 11, row ALIGNmling, columns en/de/fr/cs (90.2, 84.1, 84.9, 63.2); M3P zero-shot 57.9, 36.8, 27.1, 20.4

results.claim: Image+text queries by adding embeddings enable multimodal search
results.setup: Qualitative, 160M CC-BY image index, text embedding weight 2 and image weight 1 (1:1 also works)
results.note: No quantitative evaluation; figure examples only.

limits: Dataset is not released and its filtering thresholds are given but the crawl is not reproducible
No training compute, wall-clock, or parameter counts are given
Most results are single runs without variance
Authors note intra-modal (text-text, image-image) performance is weaker and suspect the cross-modal-only objective; multitask training left to future work
Social impact section: harmful alt-text, stereotypes, no fairness analysis done; further analysis needed before production use
Ablations use a smaller B5+BERT-base or B7+BERT-base at reduced steps; the noisy-vs-clean comparison is on COCO zero-shot only
